status_summary: Executive Order 14162 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-30) directed ending financial commitments made under the UN climate framework and revoked the U.S. International Climate Finance Plan. A letter dated 2025-03-04 announced that the US board member and alternate on the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage were stepping down and would not be replaced by a US representative. A presidential memorandum signed 2026-01-07 directed withdrawal from the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, and the UN depositary recorded that withdrawal on 2026-02-27, effective 2027-02-27. The sources reviewed do not show efforts to persuade other countries to reconsider their contributions.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14162 published; section 3 directs revoking UN climate framework financial commitments and revokes the International Climate Finance Plan.

Presidential memorandum directed withdrawal from listed international bodies, including the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, defined for UN entities as ending participation and funding; published 2026-01-16.
The UN depositary recorded the U.S. withdrawal from the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (notification C.N.102.2026.TREATIES-XXVII.7), effective 2027-02-27.

title: Refuse climate reparations and exit the UN loss and damage fund
uncertainties: The board withdrawal letter is documented by a Columbia Law School tracker page (undated, which links the letter through an archive service that refused automated fetching) an E&E News report of 2025-03-10 that dates the letter March 4 and names a Treasury Department official on the fund board as its sender, and a PTI wire report of 2025-03-07 that describes the letter as sent on behalf of the Treasury Department and saying the board member and alternate are stepping down, not to be replaced by a US representative; neither the letter nor an official State, Treasury or fund secretariat document was read. The 2026 memorandum does not name the loss and damage fund. Whether any US pledge to the fund was paid was not checked. A House Appropriations Democratic summary says the final FY2026 State and foreign operations bill dropped the House ban on funding loss and damage compensation, and a similar summary says the House FY2027 bill (H.R. 8595, passed the House 2026-07-15, received in the Senate 2026-07-29) bars it; the text of the engrossed H.R. 8595 was searched in part and the provision was not located, and neither bill is shown as enacted with such a rider. No fund board decision on US membership was found. The Federal Register search for loss and damage after 2026-01-08 returned only unrelated documents.
